extracted.intended_audience: persons and organizations filing petitions with NHTSA (manufacturers, safety advocates, legal counsel, engineers, interested members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive content requirements for petitions to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration requesting rulemaking or defect/noncompliance orders, including general filing rules and a special expedited-subpart for DASS test procedures under FMVSS No. 208.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (§552.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part establishes procedures for the submission and disposition of petitions filed by interested persons pursuant to 49 U.S.C. Chapters 301, 305, 321, 323, 325, 327, 329 and 331 to initiate rulemaking or to make a decision that a motor vehicle or item of replacement equipment does not comply with an applicable Federal motor vehicle safety standard or contains a defect which relates to motor vehicle safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§552.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable NHTSA to identify and respond on a timely basis to petitions for rulemaking or defect or noncompliance decisions, and to inform the public of the procedures following in response to such petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (Any interested person) (§552.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may file with the Administrator a petition requesting commencement of a proceeding to issue/amend/revoke a motor vehicle safety standard or to decide whether to issue an order concerning notification and remedy of noncompliance or a defect relating to motor vehicle safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: General filing requirements for a petition (§552.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition must: (a) be written in English; (b) have, preceding its text, a heading that includes the word 'Petition'; (c) set forth facts which it is claimed establish that an order is necessary; (d) set forth a brief description of the substance of the order which it is claimed should be issued; and (e) contain the name and address of the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should be addressed/submitted to Administrator, NHTSA, 400 Seventh Street, S.W., Washington, DC 20590.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improperly filed petitions (§552.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A petition not addressed as specified in §552.4 but meeting other requirements will be treated as properly filed when discovered and identified. (b) A document failing to conform to one or more requirements of §552.4(a)-(e) will not be treated as a petition under this part and will be handled as correspondence or other procedures at NHTSA's discretion; suggestions may be considered at the Administrator's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonconforming submissions are not formal petitions and will not invoke petition procedures unless corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical review (§552.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriate Associate Administrator conducts a technical review of the petition, which may analyze submitted material and information already in agency possession, and may include collection of additional information or a public meeting under §552.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical review can include internal data analysis, requests for additional information, and convening public meetings if helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meeting procedures (§552.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Associate Administrator decides a public meeting would contribute to determining whether to commence a proceeding, the agency issues a Federal Register notice advising time, place, and subject matter and invites participation. Interested persons may present oral or written views and evidence; there is no cross-examination. A transcript is kept and exhibits may be accepted; sections 556 and 557 of title 5, U.S.C., do not apply. The Chief Counsel designates a legal officer to serve at the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings are informational with transcript/exhibits; no adjudicative procedures (no cross-examination) and certain APA adjudicative sections do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of agency action on petition (§552.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: After technical review and taking into account appropriate factors (which may include allocation of agency resources, agency priorities, and likelihood of success in litigation which might arise from the order), the Administrator will grant or deny the petition. NHTSA will notify the petitioner of the decision within 120 days after its receipt of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency considers resource allocation, priorities, litigation risk, and other appropriate factors when deciding; 120-day notification target from receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of petition (§552.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If a petition for rulemaking is granted, a rulemaking proceeding is promptly commenced in accordance with applicable NHTSA and statutory procedures; granting does not guarantee the rule will be issued. (b) If a petition regarding noncompliance or defect is granted, a proceeding to determine existence of noncompliance or defect is promptly commenced via investigation by the Office of Standards Enforcement or Office of Defects Investigation, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant initiates formal proceedings/investigations but final outcomes depend on the subsequent process and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of petition (§552.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is denied, a Federal Register notice of the denial is issued within 45 days of the denial, setting forth the reasons for denial of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial must be publicly explained via FR notice within 45 days of the denial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application — Subpart B scope (Expedited DASS test procedure petitions) (§552.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes procedures for submission and disposition of petitions filed by interested parties to initiate rulemaking to add a test procedure to 49 CFR 571.208, S28 (Dynamic Automatic Suppression System test procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for Subpart B (DASS, ASZ, Standard No. 208) (§552.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Dynamic automatic suppression system (DASS) means a portion of an air bag system that automatically controls whether or not the air bag deploys during a crash by (1) sensing occupant location, (2) interpreting occupant characteristics/location to determine deployment, and (3) activating or suppressing the air bag. (b) Automatic suppression zone (ASZ) means a three-dimensional zone adjacent to the air bag cover, specified by the vehicle manufacturer, where air bag deployment will be suppressed by the DASS if a vehicle occupant enters the zone under specified conditions. (c) Standard No. 208 means 49 CFR 571.208.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the technical terms used throughout Subpart B and the petition content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of petition for DASS test procedures (§552.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition under this subpart shall: (a) be submitted to Administrator, NHTSA (address given); (b) be written in English; (c) state petitioner name and address; (d) set forth in full the data, views and arguments supporting the requested test procedure, including all content information specified by §552.14 and any documents incorporated by reference; (e) specify and segregate any information petitioner wishes withheld from public disclosure per part 512 (including, if requested, name and address of petitioner); (f) not request confidential treatment for the requested test procedure and, if confidential treatment is requested for particular DASS or supporting data/analysis, provide a general non-confidential description of the DASS operation and supporting data/analysis; (g) set forth a requested effective date and be submitted at least nine months before that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must include complete supporting material, follow confidentiality procedures in part 512, and be filed at least nine months before requested effective date. Any incorporated documents must be submitted with petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required for DASS test-procedure petitions (§552.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner shall provide: (a) a set of proposed test procedures for S28.1–S28.4 of Standard No. 208 appropriate for assessing a particular DASS, with specific positional and procedural details for each S28.x; (b) a complete description and explanation of the particular DASS (including logic, flow charts, reaction time, time duration for evaluation, performance changes by occupant size/vehicle speed, size/shape of ASZ, and discrimination between torso/head vs hand/arm vs inanimate objects); (c) analysis and data supporting appropriateness, repeatability, reproducibility and practicability of each proposed test procedure (with subrequirements for dummy-position justification for S28.1/S28.2 and extensive test method, instrumentation, video, and data requirements for S28.3/S28.4); and (d) analysis concerning the variety of potential DASS designs for which the requested test procedure is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subrequirements include: for S28.1 specify at least one 5th percentile female dummy position outside but adjacent to ASZ and representative of likely unbelted occupant; for S28.2 specify positions for 3-year-old and 6-year-old child dummies outside but adjacent to ASZ and representative of likely unbelted occupant positions during crashes with pre-crash braking; for S28.3/S28.4 provide test-device descriptions/drawings/instrumentation, means to determine suppression before device enters ASZ, means to determine when device occupies ASZ; provide basis for dummy positions, complete explanation to ascertain suppression/activation, methods to move test device at representative speeds, procedure for locating test device including reference points, methods to measure suppression timing, high-speed film/video of at least two tests, and data from at least two tests including monitored data streams and complete samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of DASS petitions (§552.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) NHTSA will process any petition that contains the information specified by this subpart; if information is missing, NHTSA will not process the petition but will advise the petitioner of needed information and seek to notify of any deficiency within 30 days after receipt. (b) At any time during consideration the Administrator may request additional supporting information and/or demonstration of requested test procedures and will seek to make such request within 60 days after receipt; demonstrations may be at an agency-designated facility or one chosen by petitioner provided facility is in North America; if request not honored to agency satisfaction, petition will not receive further consideration until requested information is submitted. (c) The agency will publish in the Federal Register either a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking proposing adoption of requested test procedures (possibly with changes) or a notice denying the petition and will seek to issue either notice within 120 days after receipt of a complete petition; this time may be extended while awaiting requested additional information or demonstration. The agency contemplates a 30–60 day comment period for any NPRM and will endeavor to issue a final rule within 60 days thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing includes target timelines (30-day deficiency notice, 60-day request-for-info window, 120-day target to publish NPRM/denial after complete petition), geographic restriction on demonstrations (North America), and potential extensions while agency awaits information. Failure to provide requested demonstrations/information halts consideration.
